tex_content.html:
\begin{example} \end{example}[the potential for constant-curvature warped products]

Source: petersen:page-0146, petersen:page-0147 ↗ prop:pet-ch4-hess-f-conformal ↗ prop:pet-ch4-snk-constant-curvature 1. ch4:4.3.2For $dr^2+\mathrm{sn}_k^2(r)ds_{n-1}^2$, with $f$ the antiderivative of $\mathrm{sn}_k$ vanishing at $r=0$: when $k=0$, $f=\tfrac 12r^2$ and $\mathrm{Hess}\, f=g$; when $k\ne 0$, $f=\tfrac 1k-\tfrac 1k\mathrm{cs}_k(r)$ and $\mathrm{Hess}\, f=\mathrm{cs}_k(r)\, g=(1-kf)\, g$. In particular, $k=1$ gives $f=1-\cos r$, $\mathrm{Hess}\, f=(1-f)g$, and $k=-1$ gives $f=\cosh r-1$, $\mathrm{Hess}\, f=(1+f)g$. \end{example}
